v05-le-bistro-de-l-h-tel.name: Le Bistro de l'Hôtel
tags: House table of the five-star Hôtel le Cep
v05-le-bistro-de-l-h-tel.why: House table of the five-star Hôtel le Cep. To order: whole roast poularde de Bresse for two; Charolais côte de bœuf. A small panelled room doing one thing supremely — the whole Bresse hen, carved at the table. The address for poultry without driving to the Bresse.

v09-loiseau-des-vignes.name: Loiseau des Vignes
tags: Bernard Loiseau group — the wine-by-the-glass bistro
v09-loiseau-des-vignes.why: Bernard Loiseau group — the wine-by-the-glass bistro. To order: œufs en meurette; pâté en croûte; 32 Burgundies poured by the glass from four oak cellars. The Saulieu three-star group's Beaune address. The point is the glass list — 32 wines kept properly, the way to drink across the Côte in one sitting. Its gougères are a benchmark. Closed Sun–Mon.

v12-march-aux-vins.name: Marché aux Vins
tags: Self-guided tasting cellar in the former Cordeliers church
v12-march-aux-vins.why: Self-guided tasting cellar in the former Cordeliers church. To order: Découverte (5 wines) 25 € or Prestige (7 wines) 49 € — taste as you walk the chapels. Three intact Gothic chapels turned tasting cellar, vintages stored 40 years underground. Go at opening, 10:00 on a weekday, when the stone is cold and empty.

v13-patriarche-p-re-fils.name: Patriarche Père & Fils
tags: The largest cellars in Burgundy — 5 km of galleries
v13-patriarche-p-re-fils.why: The largest cellars in Burgundy — 5 km of galleries. To order: the self-guided cellar visit with a tasting of 6 wines, 25 €. Founded 1780, the galleries dug under a former Visitandine convent — around two million bottles ageing in the dark. The clearest sense of how much wine sleeps beneath Beaune. Verify hours before going.

v14-bouchard-p-re-fils.name: Bouchard Père & Fils
v14-bouchard-p-re-fils.why: Cellars inside a 15th-century royal fortress. To order: the guided fortress-cellar visit and tasting; the Beaune Grèves 'Vigne de l'Enfant Jésus'. Bouchard took the Château de Beaune — built for Louis XI — in 1820; the cellars run 10 m into the rampart, holding 19th-century bottles. Book ahead; tours Tue–Sat.
